mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES signals weaker weekday commuting and fewer incidental shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will fall further over the next four weeks as reduced trip chaining suppresses retail footfall.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -22.0 to -41.4 while TRANSIT fell from -27.6 to -36.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below its prior two-week average.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and rises above 12 points, people substitute home-based activity for discretionary outings, which lowers retail visits within one week and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 12 and stays there for at least 1 week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 13.3 at t-0w after holding near 9.6-9.7 previously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 1 week after RESIDENTIAL crosses 12 and remains above that level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below their recent two-week averages indicates broad mobility compression rather than mode substitution, which reduces retail access and pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both posted their weakest weekly means at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below their prior two-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility keeps falling after a local peak, discretionary outdoor leisure is being displaced rather than expanded, and retail visits will continue to soften over the next two weeks as leisure trips do not spill into shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls at least 3 points week-on-week from an already negative level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -36.7 to -40.1 in the latest week after a brief rebound
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves within 2 weeks after a further week-on-week drop in PARKS of 3 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES predicts a delayed drop in retail mobility because access constraints and fewer in-person obligations cut shopping trips with a one- to four-week lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 while WORKPLACES falls below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further over the next 4 weeks after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move below -35.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more non-discretionary errand traffic, which partially substitutes for retail trips; if grocery mobility stays below -15, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays below -15 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped to -16.3 at t-0w after -12.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within 2 weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -15 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When residential staying-in and workplace avoidance occur together, people batch errands less often and shift spending online, so RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 12 while WORKPLACES falls below -30
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 13.3 and WORKPLACES fell to -41.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its previous 28-day average after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 12 and WORKPLACES is below -30.

mechanism_narrative: If transit remains deeply negative while parks and retail both weaken, the city is in a low-footfall regime where destination visits are suppressed across categories; RETAIL_REC will stay below its recent four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 and PARKS remains below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean even though TRANSIT stays below -30 and PARKS stays below -35.
